one_line_reason: Two clean single-ingredient placebo-controlled RCTs show oral holy basil (Ocimum sanctum) leaf/extract improves glycemic control in diabetes and cognitive/stress parameters in healthy adults, with supporting mentions in broader diabetes reviews.

selected.intervention: holy basil (Ocimum sanctum) leaves, oral, randomized placebo-controlled crossover
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (leaves, specific gram dose not given)
selected.primary_outcome: fasting and postprandial blood glucose, serum cholesterol
selected.why_selected: clean single-ingredient, placebo-controlled crossover trial with a significant, quantified glucose reduction (~17.6% fasting, ~7.3% postprandial).

selected.intervention: ethanolic holy basil (Ocimum sanctum) leaf extract, oral capsules, 30 days
selected.primary_outcome: cognitive performance (Sternberg and Stroop test reaction time/error rate, P300 latency), salivary cortisol, anxiety
selected.why_selected: second clean single-ingredient RCT with a clear dose, showing improved cognitive parameters versus placebo in a healthy (non-clinical) population.

selected.population: adults with type 2 diabetes (Cochrane systematic review, 66 RCTs, 8302 participants, 69 different herbal medicines)
selected.intervention: holy basil leaves, oral, among many herbal medicines compared to placebo
selected.why_selected: an authoritative Cochrane review explicitly names holy basil leaves as showing a significant hypoglycemic response versus placebo, corroborating the dedicated single-ingredient diabetes RCT.

selected.population: adults aged 18-65 with high perceived stress (n=186, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled)
selected.intervention: multi-herb formula (Rhodiola, holy basil, and Schisandra chinensis; VL-G-A57), oral, 60 days
selected.primary_outcome: Perceived Stress Scale score; sleep quality, mood, anxiety
selected.why_selected: large, well-powered recent (2026) RCT adding a stress-related outcome, though holy basil is only one of three herbs in the tested formula.

blockers: The Cochrane diabetes review (15266492) gives only a brief, non-dosed mention of holy basil within a review of 69 different herbal medicines, so the specific trial(s) behind that claim would need to be traced and verified separately.
The most recent, best-powered positive trial (41656269) tests holy basil only as one of three herbs in a fixed combination (with Rhodiola and Schisandra), so its own contribution cannot be isolated.

The two clean single-ingredient RCTs are decades apart (1996 and 2015), target different outcomes (glycemic control in diagnosed diabetes vs. cognition/stress in healthy adults), and neither gives a precise leaf/extract dose in mg that can be directly mapped to catalog labels.

excluded_pmids.reason: Broad systematic review of 25 different plants/phytonutrients and their effects on HPA-axis hormones; holy basil's own result is not detailed, and the review concludes effects are largely 'unclear' for most phytonutrients other than ashwagandha.

Broad review of Ayurvedic herbs for diabetes covering many different herbs and formulas; mentions holy basil as showing a glucose-lowering effect worth further study but gives no dose or effect-size detail, redundant with the more specific Cochrane review already selected.
Holy basil essential oil tested as one ingredient in a topical antiwrinkle body cream blend; a topical cosmetic application, not an oral supplement.

RCT of a 9-ingredient multi-herb supplement (holy basil one of nine) for cognitive function in older adults; effect cannot be isolated to holy basil, and the trial's headline finding was actually a memory deficit, with only processing-speed showing improvement.
Prolonged-fasting RCT where holy basil herbal tea is merely one allowed beverage within a 500 kcal/day fasting diet; not a holy basil supplementation trial and entirely confounded with fasting.
